cryptographic_operation: Generate an RSA consent authority identity
migration_objective: Replace RSA authority provisioning with ML-DSA-65 keys and update key ownership.
preconditions: Subjects, studies, and consent scopes are synthetic.
expected_behavior: Authorization is allowed only for the matching subject, study, permitted scope, and unexpired active grant.
Revocation blocks subsequent access checks and retains its reason and timestamp.
Consent identity, revision, and expiry are protected by the authority signature.
migration_requirements: Use ML-DSA-65 with a CareConsent-specific context.
Update stored signatures and public-key encodings without fallback to RSA.
Preserve fail-closed authorization and revocation behavior.
verification_procedure: Run original and PQC test modules independently.
Exercise authorization positive/negative cases, expiry, revocation, invalid record, signature and serialization behavior.
known_limitations: Synthetic consent only; this is not a clinical consent system or legal compliance certification.
